_note: Example commands a user can make. None of these run on their own: they're starting points offered in Create Command and doit create. Only examples that suit the PC are offered: 'os' (any of these OS IDs, from /etc/os-release ID or ID_LIKE), 'not_os' (none of these) and 'needs' (programs that must be installed). Verify each against the book before relying on it.

examples.explanation: Shows how full each drive is, in sizes that are easy to read.

examples.command: sudo pacman -Sy --needed archlinux-keyring cachyos-keyring && sudo pacman -Su
examples.explanation: Refreshes the package signing keys first, then updates everything installed. Keys go stale on a system that hasn't updated in a while, and installs fail until they're refreshed.
examples.warning: This updates your whole system, including the kernel. Take a snapshot first if you want an undo button.

examples.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade
